UPDATE: Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Explosive allegations from the KwaZulu Natal Police Commissioner send shock waves through government and civil society.

Unique Selling Point:
We interviewed Mkhwanazi in 2024 about his apparently tough on crime stance - we revisit the man behind this week's shock revelations.

Summary:
This week, KwaZulu Natal Provincial Police Commissioner Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi called a press conference about the work of a task team formed in 2018 to focus on political killings. But what looked like a status update quickly developed into a series of bombshell allegations. Mkhwanazi claimed that Police Minister Senzo Mchunu has frozen investigations and attempted to disband the task team because it uncovered links between drug cartels and political leadership. He also accused senior officials of interfering in investigations into political assassinations. The allegations have sent shock waves through civil society and government. The judiciary has demanded evidence, while Mchunu denies any wrongdoing. But who is Mkhwanazi? We sat down with him last year to discuss his controversial reputation.

Script:


(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) I'm here this morning in order to speak to you about the policing issues that are happening in KZN as well as in the Republic of South Africa.
(Narrator) This week, KwaZulu Natal Provincial Police Commissioner Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi called a press conference about the work of a task team formed in 2018 to focus on political killings.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) The team has been investigating a total of 612 case dockets. These case dockets include murders, attempted murders, intimidation, conspiracy to commit murders and other cases.
(Narrator) But what looked like a status update quickly developed into a series of bombshell allegations.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) On the 26th of March 2025, this year, a total of 121 case dockets that were under investigation were taken away from the task team.
(Narrator) Mkhwanazi claimed that Police Minister Senzo Mchunu has frozen investigations and attempted to disband the task team because it uncovered links between drug cartels and political leadership.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) Amongst others, politicians who are currently serving in Parliament... members of the South African Police Service, the Metro Police and Correctional Services. They include prosecutors in Gauteng Province, the judiciary. And all these are controlled by the drug cartel.
(Narrator) He also accused senior officials of interfering in investigations into political assassinations. The allegations have sent shock waves through civil society and government.
(Deputy Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya/Newzroom Afrika) He doesn’t know what he’s talking about.
(Ian Cameron/SABC News) The allegations are very very serious.
(Dereleen James/Newzroom Afrika) I am disgusted but I cannot say that we are surprised.
(Leigh-Ann Mathys/SABC News) People must be fired, people must go to prison and we must clean up the system.
(President Cyril Ramaphosa) It is a serious matter, it has to do with the security of our people, but it also has to do with our adherence to the rule of law.
(Narrator) The judiciary has demanded evidence, while Mchunu denies any wrongdoing. But who is Mkhwanazi? We sat down with him last year to discuss his controversial reputation.
(Govan Whittles) It seems like you’re encouraging the police to shoot?
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) I’m encouraging them not to die with their weapons in their hands.
(Narrator) Mkhwanazi has served the police for decades, beginning with public order policing and later heading the elite Special Task Force.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) My intention has always been when I joined the service that I would want to go into the tactical unit, I wanted to learn how to fight the criminals. I just wanted to be in a coal face of the crime fighting
(Govan Whittles) How was it?
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) It was a lot of fun. Task force has always been about fun.
(Narrator) As Provincial Commissioner, he’s known for his hands-on approach.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) I always believe that until you understand what the client needs, you will never be able to service them. And the clients are not in the office. The clients are on the street. The clients are in their own houses. So we ought to be there.
(SABC News) Three suspects shot dead…
(Newzroom Afrika) At least four people have been killed...
(Narrator) But he’s also been criticised for pitting police in a literal war against crime. It’s an approach he defends vehemently.
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) I'm not going to discourage police officers to protect themselves and the citizens. The question is, why don't you make the laws to be more tighter, to make sure when this person is arrested he doesn't go back to society again?
(Narrator) This week is not the first time Mkhwanazi has gone public with his concerns about the country’s state of lawlessness. But will he survive the fallout?
(Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi) My families are spread across different provinces. So it is my duty, and the fellow police officers, to protect them. So I'm not going to surrender their freedom. I'm not going to surrender their safety to anyone. So I will die for this badge. I will die for them. So I will fight this fight until the end. Wherever the end is, we will fight.
